questions.skill: Give informal arguments for the triangle angle sum and the exterior angle of a triangle
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Three copies of the same triangle are placed side by side so that its three different angles meet at one point, with no gaps or overlaps, along a straight line. Explain why this shows that the angles of the triangle add to 180°.
questions.prompt_markup:
Three copies of the same triangle are placed side by side so that its three different angles meet at one point, with no gaps or overlaps, along a straight line.
Explain why this shows that the angles of the triangle add to 180°.
questions.correct_answer: The three angles fill a straight angle, so they add to 180°.
questions.required_method: The three angles, one of each kind, together fill a straight angle, which measures 180°. So angle A + angle B + angle C = 180°. Any equivalent explanation is accepted.

questions.skill: Give informal arguments for the triangle angle sum and the exterior angle of a triangle
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In the figure, the line through B is parallel to AC. Use angles 1, 2, and 3 to explain why the angles of triangle ABC add to 180°.
questions.prompt_markup: In the figure, the line through B is parallel to AC. Use angles 1, 2, and 3 to explain why the angles of triangle ABC add to 180°.
questions.correct_answer: Angle A + angle B + angle C = 180°
questions.required_method: Angle 1 = angle A and angle 3 = angle C (alternate interior angles, because the line is parallel to AC). Angles 1, 2, and 3 together form a straight angle, so angle A + angle B + angle C = 180°.

questions.skill: Give informal arguments for the triangle angle sum and the exterior angle of a triangle
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Use the triangle angle sum to explain why the exterior angle at C of triangle ABC equals angle A + angle B.
questions.prompt_markup: Use the triangle angle sum to explain why the exterior angle at C of triangle ABC equals angle A + angle B.
questions.correct_answer: The exterior angle at C = angle A + angle B
questions.required_method: The exterior angle and angle C form a linear pair, so exterior angle = 180° - angle C. The triangle's angles add to 180°, so angle A + angle B = 180° - angle C. Therefore exterior angle = angle A + angle B.

sections.skill: Prove theorems about isosceles and right triangles

questions.skill: Prove theorems about isosceles and right triangles
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has AB = AC. Prove that angle B = angle C. (Use the reflection across the line that bisects angle A.)
questions.prompt_markup: Triangle ABC has AB = AC. Prove that angle B = angle C. (Use the reflection across the line that bisects angle A.)
questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Other valid orders are accepted. A conclusion without reasons is not full credit. Example: the reflection across the bisector of angle A maps ray AB onto ray AC; since AB = AC, it maps B to C (and C to B). So it maps triangle ABC onto itself and angle B onto angle C; reflections keep angle measures, so angle B = angle C.

sections.skill: Use the triangle angle sum to prove angle facts about parallelograms

questions.skill: Use the triangle angle sum to prove angle facts about parallelograms
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In parallelogram ABCD, diagonal AC is drawn. Prove that angle B = angle D. Give a reason for each step.
questions.prompt_markup: In parallelogram ABCD, diagonal AC is drawn. Prove that angle B = angle D. Give a reason for each step.
questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Other valid orders are accepted. A conclusion without reasons is not full credit. Example: angle BAC = angle DCA (alternate interior angles, AB ∥ DC); angle BCA = angle DAC (alternate interior angles, BC ∥ AD); in each triangle the angles add to 180°, so angle B = 180° - angle BAC - angle BCA = 180° - angle DCA - angle DAC = angle D.

questions.correct_answer: x = 40; angle A = angle C = 120° and angle B = angle D = 60°.
